newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan Jan long-term prime to be unchanged - banker.
newsitem.headline: Japan Jan long-term prime to be unchanged - banker.

text.p: Japan's long-term prime rate is likely to stay at a record low of 2.5 percent in January, a long-term credit bank source said on Monday.
A further fall in the Japanese bond market could, however, cause the long-term prime rate to be raised, the source added.
The Industrial Bank of Japan Ltd (IBJ) will officially announce its long-term prime rate and the coupon rate for January five-year bank debentures on Wednesday, an official at the bank said.
The January long-term prime rate will come into effect on Friday, the official added.
The prime rate, at which long-term credit banks lend to their most creditworthy customers, was cut by 0.2 percentage point to a historical low of 2.5 percent in December.
The IBJ customarily sets its long-term prime rate 0.9 percentage point above its debenture coupon rate.
The yield of IBJ bank debentures issued in December with a coupon rate of 1.6 percent stood at around 1.79 percent in Monday morning trade, a trader for a brokerage house said.
